title: Paired HARPS fits do not resolve a Ross 128 second-harmonic extraction difference at 9.8556 days
abstract: We test the second harmonic of the known Ross 128 planet in 305 HARPS-RVBank version 02 exposures. A paired DRS minus SERVAL fit at a fixed 9.8556-day orbit period gives an amplitude of 0.219 m/s. Four conditional group-sign tests give tail fractions of 0.264 to 0.346. Eleven model controls also do not resolve a difference. Recovery of an added 0.3 m/s difference is only 22 to 54 percent under the tested noise rules. Thus the result cannot establish agreement or remove small processing effects. It does not confirm an eccentric orbit, find a new planet, or identify a physical cause. The reductions share spectra. No independent-instrument data are fitted. The package has original code, aggregate results, a figure, exact source hashes and external retrieval steps. Source records remain outside the publication.

display.caption: Second-harmonic coefficients and conditional tail fractions. Crosses show main fits. Small dots show controls. All main tests stay above the 0.01 reference line. These are conditional diagnostics.
